text: Ketu takes its turn as antardasha, the smaller period each lord gets inside the major one, and the Moon's ten-year chapter of home and care goes quiet for a while. Ketu is the Moon's south node, one of the two points where eclipses form, and it works by subtraction. Attachments loosen. Interest in the household can thin out, not from anger but from a change of appetite, and things you once needed around you begin to feel optional. The past comes up through the floor. Childhood rooms, people you have not thought about in years, a grief you got through by staying busy: this stretch tends to bring them back for another look. Some people leave a place that no longer fits. Others step back from a caretaking role held well past its term, or find that the role simply ends. Solitude stops feeling like a punishment, and sleep and dreams get louder than usual. The cost is worth naming. Withdrawal reads as coldness to people who count on your warmth, and a quiet mood is easy to mistake for indifference, so a little explaining goes a long way in this run. Your body may also ask for less noise than your schedule allows. Nothing here is a judgment on the people you love. What this run lets go of is usually something you had already outgrown, and you come out needing fewer props in order to feel at home.

Venus and the Moon get along, and this run shows it. Each major period is divided among the nine lords in a fixed order, and a sub-period is called an antardasha; Venus now holds one inside the Moon's decade of care and belonging. The keynote is ease. What was merely functional at home starts wanting to be pleasant, and people often paint, rearrange, or spend on the room where everyone actually sits. Company gets easier too. Invitations go out, the table fills, and affection has an unusual amount of room to work in. Partnerships tend to deepen here, since both lords involved care more about being close than about being right, and old family friction can settle without much of a fight. Money moves toward comfort and toward food, and the pleasure in that is not frivolous. The soft risk deserves plain statement. Comfort makes a good hiding place, agreement can stand in for a real conversation, and the wish to keep things nice will quietly shelve a subject that needed air. Handled with some honesty, the run works as a refill. You come out of it reminded that your life is meant to be enjoyed and not only administered, and that reminder tends to outlast the agreeable run that taught it.

A stretch of the Moon's decade now belongs to the Sun. The larger period runs ten years on home, mood, and care; inside it each lord in turn holds an antardasha, a sub-period with its own flavor, and this one is the Sun's. Private life picks up a public edge. Work you have done quietly for a household, for a relative, or for a small group that leans on you tends to come into view, and some people are handed a title or a standing that grows straight out of it. The pairing also raises a blunt question. In a decade organized around what other people need, what do you want? This is the run where that question stops being rhetorical, and where the wanting usually has to be said out loud before anything moves. Figures of authority in the family often feature: a parent or whoever filled that place, an elder whose approval still carries weight, an inheritance in the broad sense of the word. Physical energy generally picks up, and it is worth spending on something that carries your own name. The friction is between the two roles. Pride and softness pull different directions, and it is possible to defend a position at home that you do not actually hold. At its best the run puts a self back at the middle of all that caring.

The Moon's decade opens with the Moon's own turn. Inside every major period the nine lords each govern an antardasha, a sub-period of their own, and the first belongs to the lord of the whole chapter, so the theme arrives undiluted. Whatever the next ten years are about, this opening run introduces it. Home comes to the front. Many people move, rebuild, take someone in, or change what the word family covers, and the arrangement made now tends to set the terms for everything that follows. Whoever cared for you early, parent or not, often figures in the story, through closeness, through care needed, or through a new understanding of what they passed on. Feeling runs near the surface. You register other people's states quickly, remember more than you want to, and take things in deeply, which is good for intimacy and hard on your defenses. The body keeps the same tides, so rest, appetite, and the shape of your days become subjects you cannot ignore. The main hazard is treating weather as climate. A low week looks permanent from the inside, and a decision made at the bottom of the tide rarely survives the top of it, so the moods want time to finish their sentences. What this stretch establishes is a baseline: where you live, who feeds whom, and what returns you to yourself when nothing else does.

Mars has no talent for keeping the peace, and it now holds an antardasha, one lord's stretch of the Moon's ten-year chapter of home and care. The chapter's concerns are domestic; this lord is not. The household tends to get physical. Repairs, building work, heavy things carried up stairs, a sudden decision to fix what everyone had learned to live around: the run has energy and prefers to spend it close to home. Some people relocate on short notice. Property and shared ground can turn into a live question, and boundaries with relatives get tested, sometimes to good effect. Temper is the honest weather here. Irritation surfaces at home first, because that is where the guard comes down, and the same edge that defends your people can cut them. A sentence said in a kitchen lasts longer than one said anywhere else, which makes this a stretch to slow down in rather than one to win. Sleep can turn restless, and pushing your body past what it agreed to is a familiar hazard of the pair. There is a better version available. Mars in the Moon's territory can stand up for something that genuinely needed defending: a child, a parent, a home, your own right to rest. Courage in private life gets no audience and is often harder for that reason. Spend the heat on protection and repair, and the run leaves behind a household that knows it has been fought for.

Restlessness moves into the house. Rahu is the Moon's north node, the hungrier of the two eclipse points, and it takes an antardasha, a stretch of its own inside the Moon's long chapter of care and belonging. A node landing on the decade's own subject tends to unsettle the ground it stands on. Wanting grows. What you have starts to look small, and the unfamiliar starts to look like home: another city, another country, a circle nothing in your background prepared you for. People often move a long way in a run like this, or bring something foreign into the household, in food, in belief, in who sits at the table. Ambition can arrive suddenly in a chapter that had been about tending, and it frequently gets results. The mind is the tender spot. Sleep can go strange, worry runs without a subject attached, and appetite of every kind gets louder after dark, so anything that keeps your nights ordinary earns its keep. Restlessness is easy to read as a message about your whole life. Sometimes it is one and sometimes it is only weather, and telling them apart is most of the work. A strong pull toward a new person or a new place is not by itself evidence about either. Keep your footing and the run widens your sense of where you could belong, along with proof that a home can survive being questioned.

This is the run in the decade that most often feels like relief. Jupiter holds an antardasha, its own turn inside the ten-year chapter the Moon governs, and its subject is growth while the chapter's subject is care, so what grows tends to be the things that hold you up. The household often gets larger or simply better. A bigger place, a birth, a marriage, a student, a friend who turns into kin: this run adds people more often than it removes them. Support arrives from someone with the standing to offer it, and help given now usually comes without a hook in it. Mood lifts along with the rest. Confidence returns to parts of life that had felt like heavy lifting, and the future starts to look like something you can plan rather than something to brace for. Meaning becomes a live interest too, and many people take up study, a practice, or a tradition in this stretch and keep it long afterward. Excess comes from the same source as the gift. It is easy to take on more than the household can carry, to promise warmly and pay for it later, and to let good feeling do work that a plan should be doing. Comfort finds willing conditions here, at the table and in the accounts alike. Kept in proportion, this is where the decade banks its warmth, and you finish it with more people who would answer the phone.

The heaviest stretch of this decade usually belongs to Saturn. Its antardasha, a slower run inside the Moon's ten years, brings the plainest work of the chapter: finding out what in your private life can bear a load and what has been running on hope. The tempo slows down. Care turns into duty, in both the good and the hard sense of that word. An elder may need tending, or a house, or a person whose difficulty has no quick end, and the job is showing up on the days when nobody thanks you for it. Long commitments get signed in this run, the kind that outlast it. Mood can sit low and quiet, and many people would call what they feel in this run loneliness, sometimes inside a full house. That deserves saying without decoration, and it also deserves proportion. A heavy season is a season and not a summary of your life, and the light generally returns before the lessons do. Routine matters more now than it usually does. Regular hours, regular meals, and time with people who want nothing from you steady more than they appear able to. Old family patterns also come up for review, and this is a stretch where they can genuinely be changed rather than only noticed. What Saturn leaves is durable: boundaries you finally held, arrangements built under pressure, and the people who stayed.

Most of this run happens on the phone and at the kitchen table. Mercury's antardasha, a sub-period inside the Moon's decade of home and care, sets a quick mind to work on slow material: moods, meals, relatives, and the logistics that keep a place running. Talk multiplies. Arrangements get made and remade, forms and calls pile up around somebody's care or a change of address, and the calendar fills with small necessary things. Neighbors, cousins, and siblings or the people who stand in for them step forward now, and the traffic between houses picks up. Short trips are common, and so is a season of living partly in two places. Curiosity turns domestic as well. You may take an interest in where your family came from, in how a house actually works, in recipes and records and old photographs, and things you had only ever felt become possible to see written down. Home and commerce mix easily in this pairing, through work done where you live or a business that runs on family ties. The strain is a fast mind on material it cannot argue with. Worry runs in circles, small signals get read too closely, and you can discuss a feeling long enough to lose track of having it. What the run leaves behind is administrative and quietly large: the arrangements, the contacts, and the habit of asking instead of assuming.
